newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-RUSSIAN PAIR TEST POSITIVE FOR STEROIDS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-RUSSIAN PAIR TEST POSITIVE FOR STEROIDS.

text.p: Russia's world silver medallist walker Olympiada Ivanova and her compatriot Lyubov Tsyoma have both tested positive for steroids at the world championships and face two-year bans, team sources said on Sunday.

Ivanova, who finished second in Thursday's 10 kms walk, will also be stripped of her medal and lose $30,000 prize money. Tsyoma did not win a medal after failing to finish her 800 metres semifinal heat, also on Thursday.

The 27-year-old Ivanova, who produced the best performance of her career to win the silver medal, became the second medallist to test positive at the Athens championships which have seen a total of five positive cases so far.
Ukraine's world shot put champion Aleksandr Bagach was stripped of his gold medal after testing positive for the stimulant ephedrine.
French 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan, neither of whom made the finals, also tested positive for ephedrine.
Belarus walker Olga Kardopoltseva, who finished third, will be given the silver medal with her compatriot Valentina Tsybulskaya elevated from fourth to the bronze medal position.
